editorial:
Imagine moving into a giant, old palace in Varanasi, only to find out the place is supposedly cursed. That is exactly what happens to Siddharth and his wife, Avni. They ignore the scary warnings and move in anyway, but things quickly get weird. You will see strange noises, locked doors that open on their own, and a feeling that someone is watching them. The vibe is a great mix of spooky ghost stories and laugh-out-loud comedy. It does not just try to scare you; it keeps you guessing whether you are watching a paranormal nightmare or just a series of accidents.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the funny and quirky psychiatrist, Aditya. He brings a lot of energy to the screen and makes the mystery feel like a puzzle you want to solve. The pacing is solid, though some parts of the middle drag a bit. If you love movies with a big twist, you will love this. For the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail of the palace. Or, if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great call for movie night.
endingExplained: You find out there is no real ghost. Avni has a split personality disorder and believes she is a dancer named Manjulika. She did this because of repressed trauma from her past. Aditya tricks her into thinking the ghost is gone by staging a fake ritual. He makes her believe the spirit has been sent away, which cures her mind. Everyone is safe, the mystery is solved, and the movie ends on a happy note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves a mix of laughs and scares with a big twist.
